newsitem.title: USA: Banks must check portfolio risk continually - Moskow.
newsitem.headline: Banks must check portfolio risk continually - Moskow.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Michael Moskow said on Friday U.S. banks should assess portoflio risk on an ongoing basis due to the array of new financial products made possible by technology.

"Technology has allowed banks to offer an array of new products that can very quickly change the value of their portfolios," Moskow told the Chicago Fed's Conference on Bank Structure and Competition.

CHICAGO, May 2 (Reuter) - Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Michael Moskow said on Friday U.S. banks should assess portoflio risk on an ongoing basis due to the array of new financial products made possible by technology.

"Technology has allowed banks to offer an array of new products that can very quickly change the value of their portfolios," Moskow told the Chicago Fed's Conference on Bank Structure and Competition.
The three-day conference focused on the challenges, risks and opportunities new technologies are creating in the financial services sector.
"Precommitment has a lot of appeal to me and I think it should be given serious consideration as a preferred means of determining capital requirements," Moskow also said.
The Fed is also watching the emergence of non-regulated, non-insured new comers in the financial services sector that may heighten the risk for systemic failure.

"Who should be allowed to issue third-party payments?" Moskow asked, referring to one of the topics discussed at the conference. "It was argued yesterday that this role should be restricted to regulated depository institutions in order to maintain the integrity of the payments systems."
Summing up the findings of the Chicago Fed conference, Moskow pointed out "the industry has two options. Adapt to the new technology and the opportunities it offers or get left behind."

Other issues discussed at the conference included the need to reduce the dependence on paper checks, "a process that needs to be driven by the market, not by regulatory mandate," the Chicage Fed president stressed.
The conference also discussed technology's ability to give financial services more information about customers, and boost mortgage lending and credit availability.
